name: ocr97_night_6_nist_tech_standards
description: Night 6: NIST cybersecurity and technical standards. These documents have a distinctive NIST house style: dense paragraph text, numbered requirement sections, structured tables of controls, code-like identifiers (AC-1, IA-5, etc.), and occasional figures. Very different layout from financial PDFs. Tests whether OCR97 handles purely text-structural documents without charts.

documents.title: NIST SP 800-63B — Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Lifecycle Management
documents.goal: Extract a cybersecurity identity standard with numbered requirement sections, authenticator assurance level tables, and password policy requirements. Tests extraction of structured regulatory/technical text where section identifiers (e.g., 5.1.1) are important for document integrity.

documents.title: NIST SP 800-171r2 — Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information
documents.goal: Extract a DoD/federal contractor security requirements document with control families, requirement identifiers (3.1.1 through 3.14.7), discussion sections, and source references. Tests reading of structured requirement numbering and cross-reference tables.

documents.title: NIST SP 800-53r5 — Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems
documents.goal: Extract the first 5 pages of a 600+ page comprehensive security controls catalog. Tests the opening framework description, control families overview, and control structure definitions. One of the densest and longest NIST documents — max_pages cap is critical here.

documents.title: NIST CSWP 29 — NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
documents.goal: Extract the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 with its six Function categories (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover), Category/Subcategory tables, and implementation examples. Tests extraction of hierarchical structured tables where rows represent nested framework tiers.
